title: Integration under correlated Gaussian measure
statement:
Let $n\ge0$, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ each belong to $L^2(\gamma_n)$, where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Form a pair $(X,Y)$ by taking independent $X,W\sim\gamma_n$ and setting $Y=\rho X+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,W$. Then
\[
\int f(x)g(y)\,d\mathcal L(X,Y)(x,y)=\int f(x)\left(\int g\bigl(\rho x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,w\bigr)\,d\gamma_n(w)\right)d\gamma_n(x),
\]
where $\mathcal L(X,Y)$ is the resulting joint distribution.
